note:
Ground truth for the mis-tiering check in _lib/score.ts. Usage says what was run, never what was safe to run, so this is the only source of truth `agreement` can check a review file against.

PROVENANCE. `source: "corpus"` means this invocation was genuinely observed in a real window of this machine's Claude Code transcripts. `source: "known-risk"` means it was added because being wrong about it is expensive, whether or not anyone has run it here — a fixture built only from observed usage would never contain the dangerous invocation you have so far avoided.

NO COUNTS, DELIBERATELY. Earlier versions carried a `count` per entry. They were removed because they could not be kept re-derivable: command-path segmentation is provisional until FKA-13 moves it after `discover`, so the paths a tally emits still shift, and option-level counts were never derivable at all — the usage profile ranks command paths, not options. A number nobody can reproduce is worse than no number, and this file already produced one review finding that way. `agreement` reads binary, path, option and tier; it never read the counts.

TIERS ARE PROPOSED, NOT RATIFIED. They follow DESIGN.md's four-tier meanings but were written by a model and have not been reviewed by a person. Until they have been, `agreement` compares one model's judgement against another's, which is better than checking a table against itself and is still not ground truth. Do not quote a mis-tiering number from this file before it is reviewed.

OPTION ENTRIES ARE THE POINT. An entry with `option` labels that option on that command, scored against the option's effective tier. DESIGN.md's argument is that options are where the danger is, so a fixture of bare command paths scores a classifier only where being wrong is cheapest. Note that `swamp extension push --dry-run` is reached by a PINNED alias, not by tiering the option lower — see DESIGN.md "Pinning beats permitting".

The case this fixture most needs to cover for mis-tiering: no Bash() prefix rule can separate this from the bare publish, because the distinguishing token is an option, and the safe form outnumbers the real publish 45 to 1 in the window. But tiering the OPTION read-safe here does not, by itself, let any wrapper run it unattended: toPolicy (review.ts) filters a command by its OWN tier — modify — before it ever looks at an option's tier, so a modify-tiered command stays unreachable from a safe-ceiling wrapper regardless of what this table says about --dry-run. The real mechanism DESIGN.md names for this ('Pinning beats permitting') is a PINNED alias, e.g. fka-write-swamp-push-dry with append:['--dry-run'] and admits.paths:[[extension,push]], permitted by settings.json naming that one wrapper even though its segment (write) is normally 'ask'. This entry still belongs in the fixture — it is real ground truth for whether the table's OWN tiering agrees with a human's — it just is not, on its own, the thing that makes the command run without a prompt.
